units.title: Chemistry: The Study of Matter
units.intro:
Chemistry studies the **composition of matter** and the **changes** it undergoes. Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space. Light, sound and heat are energy, not matter. Branches you will meet later: organic, inorganic, physical, analytical, industrial, biochemistry, environmental, nuclear.

Chemistry in life: medicines, fertilisers, fuels, plastics, soap, food additives, water treatment. That is why the book calls this a “chemical age” — not because only chemists exist, but because almost every useful object was designed with chemistry.

Properties and changes
body: **Physical property:** you can measure or see it without making a new substance (colour, density, melting point, boiling point, hardness). **Chemical property:** how it reacts (burns, rusts, reacts with acid).

**Physical change:** same substance, new form (ice→water, tearing paper, dissolving salt). **Chemical change:** new substance (burning, rusting, cooking egg). Clues: new colour, gas that is not just boiling, heat/light of its own, precipitate, hard-to-reverse.
Melting and boiling points are physical ID tags. They change with pressure (high mountain, water boils below 100 °C).

cards.title: 1.2.2 States of Matter
body: The different physical states have certain general characteristics that are true whatever chemical substance is being considered.
The three physical states show differences in the way they respond to changes in temperature and pressure.
All three show an increase in volume (an expansion) when the temperature is increased, and a decrease in volume (a contraction) when the temperature is lowered.
Liquids, on the other hand, are only slightly compressible, and the volume of a solid is unaffected by changing the pressure.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Water boils at exactly $$100^{\circ}\text{C}$$ in Massawa but at a lower temperature in Asmara. Why does this phenomenon occur?

options.A: The temperature in Asmara is lower than in Massawa.
options.B: The atmospheric pressure is lower in Asmara due to its high altitude.
options.C: The humidity is higher in Massawa.
options.D: The gravitational force is much stronger in Asmara.

cards.why:
**Step 1: Define boiling point mechanism**
Boiling occurs when the vapor pressure of a liquid equals the surrounding atmospheric pressure.

**Step 2: Compare pressures at different altitudes**
Asmara is at a high altitude, where atmospheric pressure is significantly lower than at sea level in Massawa. With lower external pressure, water molecules require less kinetic energy (lower temperature) to escape and boil.

**Step 3: Final Answer**
Therefore, the correct choice is that **the atmospheric pressure is lower in Asmara due to its high altitude**.

cards.title: Kinds of matter
body: **Pure substance:** one kind of particle. Element = one kind of atom (Fe, O₂). Compound = two or more elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio (H₂O, NaCl) — only a chemical change splits them. **Mixture:** two or more substances not chemically joined. Homogeneous (solution — same throughout). Heterogeneous (you can see bits). Separation: filtration, evaporation, distillation, magnetism, chromatography — pick the method that matches the difference (size, boiling point, magnetism…).

cards.q: Which of the following is a chemical property of carbon?

options.A: It is a black solid at room temperature.
options.C: It burns in oxygen to form carbon dioxide.

cards.why:
**Step 1: Recall the definition of chemical property**
A chemical property describes how a substance reacts chemically with other substances to form new compounds.

**Step 2: Classify the options**
Being solid, density, and solubility are physical properties. Burning in oxygen to form carbon dioxide ($$\text{CO}_2$$) is a chemical change, so flammability is a chemical property.

**Step 3: Final Answer**
The correct chemical property is **It burns in oxygen to form carbon dioxide**.

units.title: Chemical Symbols, Formulas and Equations
units.intro:
Each element has a **symbol**: one capital, second letter if any is small (Co is cobalt, CO is carbon monoxide — disaster if you mix them).

**Formula** states kinds and numbers of atoms. H₂O = 2 H + 1 O. Ionic formulas balance charges: Na⁺ with Cl⁻ → NaCl; Mg²⁺ with Cl⁻ → MgCl₂. Covalent names often use prefixes (CO₂ carbon *di*oxide).

cards.title: 3.1 Chemical Symbols
body: All "matter" in the universe is composed of elements.
A chemical symbol is a shorthand representation for the name of the element.
Many different symbols were developed over time in order to represent different substances.
The chemical symbol consists of one, two, or three letters.
The symbols for most elements are derived from their English names.

cards.title: 3.2.1 Chemical Formulas for Compounds
body: An important characteristic of a compound is that it has a chemical formula.
A chemical formula is a notation that uses chemical symbols, together with numerical subscripts to express the relative composition of the atoms of the different elements in the compound.
A molecular formula shows the number and kinds of atom present in a molecule of a compound.
A water molecule is a tightly bound unit of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

cards.title: 3.2.5 Percentage Composition
body: Just as the length of a day is made up of smaller units called hours, the mass of a compound is made up of smaller amounts of different elements.
The mass of each element in a compound compared to the total mass of the compound and multiplied by 100 is called the percentage composition of the compound.
A sample of an unknown compound with a mass of 2.37 g is extracted from the roots of a plant.
Decomposition of the sample produces 0.95 g of carbon, 1.26 g of oxygen, and 0.16 g of hydrogen.

cards.title: 3.2.6 Determining the Formula of a Compound
body: A molecular formula is the actual formula of a given compound, whereas, an empirical formula does not indicate the actual number of atoms of the elements present in the compound but rather indicates their simplest whole number ratio.
For example, the empirical and molecular formulas for carbon dioxide (CO2) and water (H2O), respectively are the same.
Determining of the Empirical Formula of a Compound.
The ratio of atoms will be the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of the elements.

**Step 1: Identify the ions and their charges**
Calcium is $$\text{Ca}^{2+}$$ and Carbonate is $$\text{CO}_3^{2-}$$.

**Step 2: Balance the charges**
Since both have a charge magnitude of $$2$$, they combine in a $$1:1$$ ratio:
$$1(+2) + 1(-2) = 0$$

**Step 3: Write the formula**
The correct chemical formula is **$$\text{CaCO}_3$$**.

cards.q: An unknown pure gas sample contains $$9.03 \times 10^{23}$$ atoms of Helium. How many moles of Helium are present in this sample?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify given variables**

body: 4.1 Scientific Method and Laboratory Safety in Chemistry

Scientific inquiry in chemistry is a systematic method of investigating the material world through controlled observation, hypothesis formulation, rigorous laboratory experimentation, and data analysis.

To safely and successfully study the transformations of matter, chemists must operate in a highly controlled environment: the laboratory. Laboratory chemistry is fundamentally different from theoretical study; it requires active hands-on experimentation, precise measurements, and strict adherence to safety protocols. cards.title: Lab / review
cards.problem: Which of the following represents the safest technique to smell an unknown gas generated during a laboratory experiment?

steps.text: Inhaling directly over a reaction vessel can cause severe respiratory damage from toxic vapors.
The standardized safe method is to hold the vessel a few inches away and wave or **waft** the vapors toward the nose with a hand.

cards.answer: Use your hand to gently waft the vapors toward your nose from a safe distance.

cards.title: Lab / review
cards.problem: When reading the liquid volume in a glass graduated cylinder, at which position should your eyes be aligned, and which part of the meniscus should be read?

steps.text: Viewing from above or below causes parallax errors in volume measurements.
To get an accurate volumetric measurement, your eyes must be directly level with the liquid surface, and you must read the value at the very **bottom of the meniscus curve**.

cards.answer: Look at eye level and read the bottom of the curved meniscus.
